title: Initial shifted-state invariant
statement: Let $A$ specify the number $n$ of items, the key bound $nb$, and the destination and counter regions, and let $it$ and $kf$ give the item and key at each index. If every item $j<n$ is stored at its stable sorting position—the number of indices $i<n$ with $kf(i)<kf(j)$ plus the number of indices $i<j$ with $kf(i)=kf(j)$—then every item remains at that position, and for every $t\le nb$ the counter cell at address $A.cnt+t$ contains the number of indices $i<n$ with $kf(i)<t$.
hypotheses_covered: The placement invariant holds for every item index j < A.n.
replaced:
Let $A$ describe $n$ items with keys $kf(j)$ and key bound $N_b$. If, for every $t<N_b$,
the counter cell at offset $t$ contains the number of indices among the first $n$ items
whose keys are below $t$, plus the number of those indices whose key equals $t$, and
every item $j<n$ occupies its sorted position $p(j)$—the number of keys below $kf(j)$
among all $n$ items plus the number of equal-key indices through $j$—then the
shifted-state conditions hold at stage $N_b$: all items occupy those sorted positions,
all counter cells at offsets $t\le N_b$ contain the number of keys below $t$, and the
waiting-cell condition for $t<N_b$ holds vacuously.
